item.description: arXiv:2607.25783v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Molecular tweezer arrays offer great prospects for quantum simulation, sensing, and computing, and would benefit from methods that enhance loading efficiency. Whereas light-assisted collisions underpin enhanced loading methods for atomic tweezer arrays, this approach cannot be directly extended to molecular arrays due to collisional loss. We show how this collisional loss can be suppressed by shelving molecules in rotationally or vibrationally excited states, so that a shelved molecule interacts with a newly loaded molecule through a repulsive van der Waals interaction. By introducing microwave assisted collisions, we show how to control the final states and the energy released in a collision between a pair of molecules. Following this controlled collision, one of the two molecules can be ejected, and we explore several strategies for ensuring deterministic ejection. Our schemes rely on currently available techniques for laser-coolable molecules, and we predict achievable filling fractions up to 96%, paving the way for scalable molecular arrays.
item.dc:creator: Etienne F. Walraven, Kang Feng, Jonas Rodewald, Michael R. Tarbutt, Tijs Karman

item.title: Ising-machine-like Driving Condition Restrictions in SSBM and Additional Pseudo-annealing- Driving Method for SSBM that Achieves Best Cut Value Search -
item.description: arXiv:2608.12545v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In our previous work, we proposed and experimentally demonstrated a physics-based simulator for combinatorial optimization problems (SSBM), which exploits a distinctive spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) phenomenon identified in a dissipative system exhibiting robust causality described by an iterative equation. We further conducted numerical simulations in which initial fluctuations of distinct patterns were applied to large-scale benchmark problems, and reported that the SSBM exhibits a unique behavior absent in conventional Ising machines: under specific conditions, pseudo-spin patterns progressively converge during the solution-search process and ultimately coalesce into a single pattern, with the cut value of the converged solution reaching 99.7% of the best-known cut value. In the present paper, we elucidate the conditions under which the SSBM can be configured to emulate the behavior of a continuous-variable Ising machine. We further demonstrate that by additionally incorporating an effect analogous to physical annealing into these conditions, the SSBM becomes capable of identifying the best-known cut value for the K_2000 benchmark instance.
item.dc:creator: Toshiya Sato

item.title: Mechanical quality factor estimation from a nonlinear optical cavity response
item.description: arXiv:2609.07393v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Intrinsic damping rate and quality factor ($Q$) are key parameters in optomechanical systems. However, in high-Q devices, their measurement is often challenging because probe-induced dynamical backaction (DBA) and the need to resolve and accurately track the mechanical resonance limit the performance of state-of-the-art techniques. Here, we introduce an all-optical ringdown method in the unresolved-sideband regime that exploits the nonlinear, time-averaged optical response induced by strong mechanical motion. We derive an analytical model of the time-averaged optical cavity response probed by a weak frequency-scanning laser. During the evolution of the mechanical oscillator, the excited motion modulates the Lorentzian lineshape into a double-horned profile whose peak separation enables an accurate estimation of the modulation amplitude. Tracking this response during the mechanical ringdown allows the intrinsic damping rate to be determined without resolving the mechanical oscillation. We apply the method to a density-modulated phononic crystal membrane placed inside a high-finesse cavity and obtain mechanical quality factors consistent with independent measurements on the same platform. Our method requires a minimal optical setup, while offering an in situ diagnostic and reduced impact from probe-induced DBA and robustness against measurement noise. Finally, the model can describe other resonant systems dispersively coupled to coherent frequency modulations, providing new insights and measurement strategies that expand beyond the optomechanical platform.
item.dc:creator: Zohran Ali, Davide Tomasella, Daniel Allepuz-Requena, Alexander Huck, Ulrik Lund Andersen

item.title: A semiconductor photon-pair source based on a polariton cascade
item.description: arXiv:2609.17900v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a theoretical study of a semiconductor photon-pair source based on a radiative cascade enabled by a permanent exciton dipole. The source consists of a GaAs quantum dot placed between a metal nanoparticle and a mirror. The dot exciton and the localized electromagnetic mode mix to form upper and lower polaritons. Without a permanent dipole, a symmetry separating states with even and odd excitation numbers forbids photon emission between the polaritons. Separation of the mean electron and hole positions gives the exciton a permanent dipole and breaks this symmetry. The upper polariton can then emit an idler photon as it decays to the lower polariton. The lower polariton can emit a signal photon as the system returns to its ground state. Using an effective model, we calculate the probability that a prepared upper polariton emits both photons through the metal antenna. We also analyze fluctuations in the emitted photon counts and correlations between the two emission channels. The calculation establishes an operating principle for assumed values of the coupling strength, emitter properties and optical loss rates. Whether the device can be built and its photon correlations measured remains open.
item.dc:creator: Karol Kawa

item.title: Interacting quantum criticality with U(1) symmetry breaking in 1+1 dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.06682v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Hohenberg-Mermin-Wagner theorem motivates the expectation that continuous symmetry remains unbroken in one-dimensional quantum ground states. Here, contrary to this expectation, we demonstrate the spontaneous breaking of U(1) spin-rotation symmetry and the emergence of an interacting quantum critical point in lattice spin-$1/2$ and spin-$1$ chains. Using subsystem Binder scaling, we locate the critical point and determine the correlation-length critical exponent as $\nu = 0.60 \pm 0.02$, distinct from the Gaussian value $1/2$ but consistent with the perturbative renormalization-group value. We further estimate the dynamical critical exponent to be $z = 1.986 \pm 0.005$ from the lowest neutral excitation gap and $z = 1.955 \pm 0.021$ from the longitudinal spin correlations. The results $z < 2$ are incompatible with microscopic realizations of this critical theory by frustration-free models, implying a mechanism for continuous symmetry breaking in one-dimensional quantum ground states distinct from frustration freeness.
item.dc:creator: Mutsumi Shimomura, Kohei Kawabata

item.title: Norm properties of quantum uniformity measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.17454v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a complete classification of the norm properties of quantum uniformity measures, introduced by Bu, Gu, and Jaffe to analytically characterize the Clifford hierarchy. Resolving an open question they posed, we show that quantum uniformity measures define norms precisely for $k=2,3,4$. In particular, we establish the triangle inequality for $k=4$, whereas for every $k\geq5$ it fails in some dimension. The higher-order result is proved using the structure theory of norming systems of linear equations over finite fields. We also study the geometry of quantum uniformity measures, establishing explicit bounds on the modulus of convexity whenever they define norms. Finally, we give a complete classification of the norm properties of matrix-valued Gowers uniformity functionals, showing that only $k=2$ defines a norm.
item.dc:creator: Berke \"Unal

item.title: Boundary-induced geometrical frustration in a square Rydberg-atom lattice
item.description: arXiv:2610.20723v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study geometric defects in square-lattice Rydberg-atom arrays induced by lattice-size parity in the striated density-wave phase. While odd-sized lattices select a single striated domain, even-sized lattices seed incompatible domains at the four corners, resulting in a {\pi}/2-rotation invariant state with a geometrical defect emanating from the lattice center. At larger detunings, we instead identify a {\pi}-rotation-invariant state with two domains nucleated by opposite corners and separated by a one-dimensional diagonal defect. We probe the state-preparation protocol on the Aquila atomic quantum processor and benchmark it with equilibrium and real-time dynamics tensor-network simulations. Our results assess the role of boundaries and lattice size in determining the global ordering in programmable quantum matter.
item.dc:creator: Marco Rigobello, Luka Pave\v{s}i\'{c}, Daniel Jaschke, Pietro Silvi, Marco Di Liberto, Simone Montangero, Simone Notarnicola

item.title: QMBL: the Quantum Many-Body Leaderboard. A live record of published ground-state energies for lattice Hamiltonians and the electron gas
item.description: arXiv:2610.22387v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In condensed matter physics, scientists explore phase diagrams of matter through various methods (analysis, numerics, experiment) and achieve consensus when enough methods agree. The quality of variational results for quantum many-body ground states is mainly judged by energy values and respective errors. Here, we present QMBL, the Quantum Many-Body Leaderboard (https://www.qmbl.org), serving as the energy layer of the scientific consensus. It is a maintained, interactive record of published ground-state energies for lattice Hamiltonians and the homogeneous electron gas. The latest release v0.5.0 holds 2511 energies on 532 instances and collects all of the community's efforts into one view. Of those instances 285 have no exact solution (164 lattice and all 121 electron-gas instances) and any new record serves as a direct improvement to an open science problem. They are the targets of a companion benchmark, QMBL: Open Problems.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Zerweck, Juan Carrasquilla

item.title: Entropy Production and Thermalization in Heavy-Quark Langevin Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.22501v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Heavy quarks are often treated as Brownian probes of the quark-gluon plasma. We formulate the irreversible entropy balance of their momentum distribution and separate the production generated by collisions from the driving caused by an evolving medium. For linear dynamics the production splits into two positive contributions, from directed momentum and from the momentum width. A static bath obeys an exact H-theorem. A cooling bath adds an explicit driving term, and longitudinal Bjorken expansion enters as a separate kinematic drive rather than as collisional production. For a Bjorken temperature protocol we derive closed-form strong- and weak-coupling limits of the total production. At strong coupling it exceeds the initial relative entropy by a term linear in the relaxation time, whose quasistatic part has the thermodynamic-length form. At weak coupling it vanishes inversely with the relaxation time. A positive strong-coupling slope therefore guarantees maximal dissipation at intermediate coupling. The same structure holds for a relativistic Fokker-Planck equation with a J\"uttner stationary state, solved numerically for charm and bottom quarks under the temperature protocol. Linear-response coefficients computed from the static generator reproduce both limits, and the numerical entropy balance is satisfied to high accuracy.
item.dc:creator: A. M. Silva

item.title: Non-planar contact structures with Calabi-Yau Fillings and topological quantum computation
item.description: arXiv:2610.25878v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper is a non-planar counterpart of the author's earlier work on planar contact structures and topological quantum computation. On a planar page every branch point is paired by a liftable arc, and the pairing matches the Ising representation exactly, in that fixing the channels of the pairs already fixes the state. Here the page has genus g and connected binding, presented as a simple degree-three cover of the disk. Every maximal system of disjoint liftable arcs then has exactly g members and leaves two branch points unused, and the half-twist interchanging the two points is not liftable, although its cube is and lifts to the identity. Ising fusion does not see that leftover pair, determining its channel from the other g and acting there only by scalars, whereas Fibonacci fusion can leave the channel undetermined. The powers of the cube then act by ten distinct relative phases on a single joint eigenspace, while the Calabi-Yau Stein filling stays fixed. An integral residue criterion supplies the Calabi-Yau test, a factorization localized on a contact connected sum is automatically Calabi-Yau, and, unlike in the planar case, a Calabi-Yau factorization need not be the shortest.
item.dc:creator: Atsuhide Mori
